title: Multiclass classification
description: One of several classes for each row: a ticket's team, a product's category.
question: Which decisions does DCLab reach on a multiclass classification problem (One of several classes for each row: a ticket's team, a product's category), and do they hold?
hypothesis: Each decision a careful data scientist reaches on this kind of problem holds on every seed of the kind's replica.
setup_summary: The multiclass classification kind's replica on seeds 0, 1, 2, brought as a person would; the five stages of the engine solve it, and each decision is checked on the finished run. No model is called.

decisions.decision: `resolved_by` is kept out of the model (the agent who closed the ticket, nearly a copy of the label)
`first_response_minutes` is kept out of the model (known only after the queue answers)
scored by macro-F1 (two teams hold 0.3 % of tickets each)
the holdout macro-F1 is 0.1 above the majority class
no copy of the label is left (holdout macro-F1 below 0.99)
the baselines the kind declares are the ones the final stage computes

claims.statement: Multiclass classification: on 3 of 3 seeds every decision held (95% interval over seeds [0.439, 1.0]); 21 of 21 decision checks held.
limitations: Invented replicas with planted traps, three seeds: what the kind decides, not how well it does on real data.
Checks on one seed share its data, so they are not independent: the interval over seeds is the honest one.
